study type: Nested case-control study within a prospective birth cohort
exposure: Maternal plasma eicosanoids (grouped by biosynthetic pathway: linoleic acid, arachidonic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, eicosapentaenoic acid; and enzyme group: cyclooxygenase, lipoxygenase, cytochrome P450)
Maternal plasma fatty acids (LA, AA, DHA, EPA)
outcome: Infant size for gestational age at delivery (Small for Gestational Age - SGA, Large for Gestational Age - LGA, Appropriate for Gestational Age - AGA)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 90 pregnant women from the LIFECODES prospective birth cohort study in Boston, Massachusetts, who delivered between 2010 and 2017, and whose infants were classified as SGA, LGA, or AGA.
finding: Maternal plasma eicosanoids from specific inflammation-related pathways (AA via CYP and LOX) and certain fatty acid precursors were significantly higher in mothers of small for gestational age (SGA) babies, while associations with large for gestational age (LGA) babies were mostly null or negative.
birth_weight: Infants were categorized as small for gestational age (?10th percentile), large for gestational age (?90th percentile), or appropriate for gestational age (>10th to <90th percentile).
gest_age: Infants were classified based on their size relative to gestational age at delivery; maternal plasma samples were collected at median 11, 25, and 35 weeks gestation.
